context.body: Genesis through Deuteronomy distinguishes requests, responses, priestly formulas, intercession, restitution, pardon, retained consequence, and stated refusal to pardon. The bounded source is Numbers 14:11–25.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Moses appeals to the proclaimed divine character, the LORD states that the people are pardoned.
observations.label: Israel is pardoned and still sentenced: action

observations.body: the unbelieving generation still receives a wilderness sentence.
observations.label: Israel is pardoned and still sentenced: response

payload.posture: Read Numbers 14:11–25 as requests, law, and pardon evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The LORD explicitly pardons Israel and then maintains the wilderness sentence; forgiveness cannot be defined as automatic removal of every outcome.
payload.title: Israel is pardoned and still sentenced
